component.name: Skimmer for Linux
component.summary: Multi-channel CW skimmer and spot feeder

description.p: A native GTK4/libadwaita CW skimmer for Linux. It pulls a wideband IQ stream from the TCI server in sdr-for-linux, splits the segment into hundreds of narrow channels with a polyphase filter bank, and decodes every signal in it at once. Validated callsigns go back to the radio as panadapter spots and out to local loggers over a CW-Skimmer-dialect telnet cluster feed.

The decoder is built for the hard half of the band, not the happy path: a soft-decision semi-Markov Viterbi lattice that carries a faded element through QSB instead of thresholding it away, a fist model that learns each operator's own spacing, a clock that re-locks in one jump when the other side of a QSO comes back at their own speed, and a tone splitter that separates two stations sharing one channel. Callsign validation is RBN-grade, so nothing unvalidated ever reaches the wire.

Built to work with its sibling apps: click a decoded callsign and the radio tunes while log-for-linux pre-fills its entry row, and calls already worked dim to gray from the logbook's duplicate service. The skimmer is read-only against the radio — it never keys, and the one deliberate write is the tuning you asked for.

First release: TCI client and IQ ingest, polyphase channelizer, the soft-decision Viterbi CW decoder with fist model and clock re-lock, RBN-grade callsign validation, station tracker and spot feeder to the panadapter, local telnet cluster feed, click-through from decoded text to radio and logbook, and duplicate-aware spot colours from log-for-linux. Decoding was validated on the air through the 2026-08-01 contest day.
